title: Yaakov Ezra Vogel v. Benjamin Moshe Vogel, Personal Representative, et al.
summary: Maryland appellate review of consolidated estate/arbitration litigation involving a Los Angeles Beth Din; the judgments were affirmed on contract/consent grounds rather than on the pleaded Beth Din misconduct allegations.

evidence.claim: The circuit court held the arbitration agreement null and void because not all necessary heirs were parties, denied confirmation, and dismissed the protective vacate/modify petition without prejudice; the Appellate Court of Maryland affirmed. The record contains allegations of refusal to hear evidence and prejudicial misconduct, but the disposition does not establish those allegations as findings.

counterevidence: The preserved misconduct/refusal-to-hear assertions were allegations in the protective petition, not adjudicated findings in the appellate disposition.
caveats: The opinion is unreported and its precedential use is limited.
Invalidity of an arbitration agreement because non-signatories did not consent is not classified as corruption.

data.question: How should Vogel v. Vogel be represented in the Beth Din civil-review corpus without turning pleaded misconduct allegations or contract invalidity into corruption findings?
data.method: Search current corpus for case and tribunal identities, review the official Maryland appellate opinion, resolve only the exact tribunal name stated in the record, and separate allegations from the judicial holding and appellate disposition.
data.framework: allegation -> adjudicated ground -> disposition -> tribunal identity -> counterevidence
data.scope: Maryland appellate civil review involving the Rabbinical Court of Cong. Agudath Israel of Los Angeles; bounded pass 3 for issue #2646
findings: The official opinion supplies an exact Los Angeles Beth Din tribunal label not previously present in the corpus search.
The protective petition alleged refusal to hear material evidence, prejudicial misconduct, and excess of powers.
The circuit court's dispositive holding instead rested on lack of agreement by necessary non-signatories; confirmation was denied and the protective petition was dismissed without prejudice.
The Appellate Court affirmed the judgments, so the record does not support converting the pleaded misconduct allegations into adjudicated misconduct findings.
conclusions: Vogel should be represented as a contract/consent enforcement decision with separately preserved but unproven misconduct allegations.
The case materially broadens the ledger beyond New York without adding a corruption finding.
limitations: The appellate opinion is unreported and subject to Maryland Rule 1-104 limitations.
This pass does not retrieve every circuit-court filing, arbitration exhibit, or tribunal governance document.
The opinion mentions an unnamed Beth Din in Israel; no identity is created for that tribunal.
unresolved: Expand the civil-review ledger across additional named tribunals and jurisdictions.
Recover authoritative governance/rules material for the exact Los Angeles tribunal if publicly available.
Continue separating adjudicated misconduct or sanctions from allegations, rejected claims, settlements, jurisdictional holdings, and ordinary enforcement disputes.
